summary: Count the set bits (Hamming weight) of an unsigned integer.
mainInsight: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so looping until n becomes 0 counts exactly the set bits (Brian Kernighan's trick) instead of testing all 32 positions.

cards.answer: Brian Kernighan's trick: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so count the iterations. Clue: It counts the set bits of the binary representation, and n & (n - 1) removes exactly one set bit per step.

promptVariants: Which operation removes the lowest set bit of n?
cards.explanation: Subtracting 1 flips the lowest set bit and all zeros below it; AND-ing with n clears that bit and keeps the higher bits.

promptVariants: Why does the loop run once per set bit?
cards.answer: Each n & (n - 1) removes exactly one 1 bit, so the number of iterations until n == 0 equals the number of set bits, independent of the zeros in between.
keyPoints: Clears one set bit per step

promptVariants: Time complexity with k set bits: ___ (at most 32).
cards.explanation: One iteration per set bit; k <= 32 so it is O(1) for fixed-width ints.

promptVariants: Brian Kernighan's bit counting uses ___ extra space.
How many iterations does n = 0 take?
cards.explanation: The loop condition `n > 0` fails immediately. The others have 1, 1 and 32 set bits.

promptVariants: Trace n = 0b1100 through the loop. What are the values of n and ans?
Step through the n & (n - 1) loop for n = 12 (0b1100).
cards.code:
ans = 0
while n > 0:
    n = n & (n - 1)
    ans += 1
cards.answer: 1100 & 1011 = 1000 (ans=1); 1000 & 0111 = 0000 (ans=2); loop ends. Each step clears the lowest 1.
cards.explanation: n - 1 flips the lowest 1 and the zeros below it.
